Rashi on Gittin 53a:12:1.hebrew: שמיה היזק - ובהיזק לא חילקה תורה, כשהוא בא בידי אדם עצמו, בין שוגג למזיד, כדאמרינן בהחובל (ב"ק דף פה:): "פצע תחת פצע", לחייב על השוגג כמזיד:
Rashi on Gittin 53a:12:1.english: Is categorized as damage - And regarding damage, when it is caused by a person himself, the Torah did not distinguish between an unintentional [act] and an intentional [act], as we say in [the chapter] HaChovel (Bava Kamma 85b): "Wound for wound" — to hold [one] liable for an unintentional [act] just as for an intentional [act]:

Rashi on Gittin 53a:12:2.hebrew: היזק שאינו ניכר - כגון הני דמתניתין, שלא נשתנו מכמות שהיו:
Rashi on Gittin 53a:12:2.english: Damage that is not evident - such as these [cases] in our Mishnah, which have not changed from what they were:

Rashi on Gittin 53a:13:1.hebrew: כדי שיודיעו - שטימא או דימע, דאי מחייבת ליה, לא אתי מודע להו לבעלים ואכלי איסורא:
Rashi on Gittin 53a:13:1.english: So that he will inform him - that he rendered [it] impure or mixed [it with terumah], for if you hold him liable, he will not come [and] inform the owners, and they will eat forbidden [food]:

Rashi on Gittin 53a:14:1.hebrew: לצעוריה קא מכוין - דאי לאו להקניטו בא ולהודיעו, למה לו דעבד:
Rashi on Gittin 53a:14:1.english: He intended to distress him - For if he did not come to vex him and to inform him, why did he do [it]?

Rashi on Gittin 53a:16:1.hebrew: הכהנים שפגלו - קרבנות ששחטום וזרקום לאכול מהם חוץ לזמנם, ולא הורצו לבעלים:
Rashi on Gittin 53a:16:1.english: The priests who rendered [an offering] piggul - [meaning] offerings that they slaughtered and sprinkled [their blood with the intention] to eat from them beyond their [allotted] time, and [thus] they were not accepted for the owners:

Rashi on Gittin 53a:16:2.english: Intentionally - that they knew that [the offerings] are disqualified thereby:

Rashi on Gittin 53a:16:3.hebrew: חייבין - לשלם דמיהן לבעלים, שהרי צריכין להביא אחרים; ואי נמי נדבה היא, קשה בעיניו שלא הקריב קרבנו, שהרי להביא דורון היה מבקש:
Rashi on Gittin 53a:16:3.english: They are liable - to pay their value to the owners, for they must bring other [offerings]; and even if it is a freewill offering, it is distressing to him that he did not offer his sacrifice, for he was seeking to bring a gift:

Rashi on Gittin 53a:16:4.hebrew: מפני תקון העולם - קס"ד דה"ק: חייבין מפני תקון העולם, שלא ירגילו בכך:
Rashi on Gittin 53a:16:4.english: For the betterment of the world - [We] initially assumed that this is what it is saying: they are liable for the betterment of the world, so that they should not make a habit of [doing] so:

Rashi on Gittin 53a:17:1.hebrew: שוגגין פטורין מפני תיקון העולם מיבעיא ליה - דהא "חייבין" דמזיד דינא דאורייתא הוא, ו"תיקון העולם" אפטורין הוא דשייך למיתני, כדי שיודיעו:
Rashi on Gittin 53a:17:1.english: It should have [stated], "[If they acted] unintentionally, they are exempt due to the betterment of the world" - For "they are liable" for an intentional [act] is Torah law, and "the betterment of the world" is relevant to teach [only] regarding "they are exempt," so that they will inform [the owner]:

Rashi on Gittin 53a:18:1.hebrew: הא שוגגין פטורין - דמתני' לא תני "שוגגין פטורין" בהדיא ברישא, ואי נמי תני "תיקון העולם", לא ארישא קאי:
Rashi on Gittin 53a:18:1.english: But [if they acted] unintentionally, they are exempt - For the Mishnah does not teach "unintentionally they are exempt" explicitly in the first clause, and even if it teaches "[for] the betterment of the world," [that] does not refer to the first clause:

Rashi on Gittin 53a:19:1.hebrew: מי חטאת - דפרה אדומה, וכן פרה עצמה, נפסלין במלאכה, דכתיב (במדבר יט): "אשר לא עלה עליה עול", ובמי חטאת כתיב: "למשמרת למי נדה"; ותניא בספרי: מה ת"ל? שיכול אין לי שתהא מלאכה פוסלת אלא בפרה, ומנין אף במים? ת"ל: "למשמרת למי נדה" — כלומר, שיהו משומרות לכך ולא לדבר אחר:
Rashi on Gittin 53a:19:1.english: Water of purification - of the red heifer, as well as the heifer itself, become disqualified through labor [performed with them], as it is written (Numbers 19): "upon which no yoke has come," and regarding the water of purification it is written: "as a safekeeping for water of sprinkling"; and it is taught in Sifrei: Why does [Scripture] state [this]? For one might think [that] I only know that labor disqualifies the heifer, and from where [do we derive that it disqualifies] the water as well? Scripture states: "as a safekeeping for water of sprinkling" — meaning, that it should be kept exclusively for this [purpose] and not for anything else:

Rashi on Gittin 53a:19:2.english: Exempt according to human laws - [from] paying:

Rashi on Gittin 53a:19:3.hebrew: וחייב בדיני שמים - פורענות לשלם לרשעים, שנתכוין להפסיד את ישראל:
Rashi on Gittin 53a:19:3.english: And [he is] liable according to the laws of Heaven - [He is subject to] retribution, to repay the wicked, because he intended to cause a loss to Israel.

Rashi on Gittin 53a:1:1.hebrew: היינו מדמע - שמערב בהיתר דבר האוסרו, וכיון דשמעינן דקנסוהו רבנן, ה"ה דילפי' מיניה למנסך, ולא אצטריך למתנייה; אבל השתא דמנסך ממש, איצטריך למתניי', דלא תימא קם ליה בדרבה מיניה ופטור:
Rashi on Gittin 53a:1:1.english: [That] is [the same as] medamea [mixing terumah] - for he mixes something that forbids it into permitted [produce]; and since we have learned that the Rabbis penalized him [for this], the same applies that we would derive [the case of] menasech [mixing idolatrous libation wine] from it, and it would not be necessary to teach it [in the Mishnah]. But now that [menasech means] actually pouring a libation [to an idol], it is necessary to teach it, so that you should not say he is subject to the greater [penalty] and is exempt [from payment]:

Rashi on Gittin 53a:20:1.hebrew: לרבקה - למקום אסיפת הבהמות וקישורן, כמו "כעגלי מרבק" (מלאכי ג):
Rashi on Gittin 53a:20:1.english: Into a pen [lirvaka] - [Meaning] to a place where animals are gathered and tethered, like "calves of the stall [marbek]" (Malachi 3):

Rashi on Gittin 53a:20:2.english: So that it would nurse - [from] its mother:

Rashi on Gittin 53a:20:3.hebrew: ותדוש - בתבואה עם השאר, דתשלומין ליכא אמעשה ידיו, דאמר: "לטובה הכנסתיה שתינק", ופסולה לא הוי אלא מחמת מחשבתו, שנתכוין אף שתדוש; וגרמא בניזקין פטור, דאמחשבה לא מחייבינן ליה, דפסולה מחמת מחשבה הוא, כדאמר (פסחים כו:): "עובד" דומיא ד"עבד", דניחא ליה:
Rashi on Gittin 53a:20:3.english: And would thresh - [Thresh] grain together with the rest [of the animals], for there is no [liability for] payment for his physical act, since he can say, "I brought it in for [its] benefit, so that it would nurse," and its disqualification only comes about because of his thought, that he intended that it should also thresh; and [since] indirect causation [gerama] in damages is exempt, we do not hold him liable for thought, as its disqualification is [only] due to thought, as it says (Pesachim 26b): "oved" [working it] is like "ubad" [it was worked], [meaning] that he is pleased with it:

Rashi on Gittin 53a:2:1.hebrew: [קנסא הוא] - מטמע ומדמע דבמזיד חייב, קנסא הוא, דהיזק שאינו ניכר לא שמיה היזק:
Rashi on Gittin 53a:2:1.english: [It is a fine] - [The liability for] rendering [another's food] ritually impure or mixing [teruma with non-sacred produce], where one is liable [when acting] intentionally, is a fine, because damage that is not discernible is not considered [actual] damage:

Rashi on Gittin 53a:2:2.hebrew: וקנסא מקנסא לא ילפינן - דהא לאו דינא הוא, והיכא דקנוס קנוס, והיכא דלא קנוס לא קנוס, ולהכי אצטריך "מנסך":
Rashi on Gittin 53a:2:2.english: And we do not derive a fine from a fine - For this [penalty] is not [a matter of] strict law; rather, where [the Sages] imposed a fine, they imposed a fine, and where they did not impose a fine, they did not impose a fine. And therefore [the case of] "one who pours [wine for idolatrous libation]" was needed [to be stated separately]:

Rashi on Gittin 53a:3:1.hebrew: ולמאן דיליף קנסא מקנסא - היינו רב, דאמר מנסך ממש, דאילו מערב לא אצטריך, דילפינן ממדמע אע"ג דקנסא הוא:
Rashi on Gittin 53a:3:1.english: And according to the one who derives a fine from a fine - this is Rav, who says [that the Mishnah refers to] one who actually pours a libation [for idolatry], for as for one who mixes [forbidden wine], it would not be necessary [to state], as we derive [it] from one who mixes teruma [with non-sacred produce], even though it is a fine:

Rashi on Gittin 53a:3:2.hebrew: כל הני - דמתני' למה לי? ליתני חדא ונילפא אידך מינה:
Rashi on Gittin 53a:3:2.english: All these - [cases] of the Mishnah, why do I need [them]? Let it teach one, and let the other be derived from it:

Rashi on Gittin 53a:4:1.english: Because he ruins it entirely - for it is no longer fit for eating:

Rashi on Gittin 53a:4:2.hebrew: דאסור לגרום טומאה - מפני פרושים שאוכלין חוליהן בטהרה, ומשום דעבד איסורא קנסוהו:
Rashi on Gittin 53a:4:2.english: For it is prohibited to cause impurity - because of [the] perushim [scrupulous individuals] who eat their non-sacred food in [a state of] purity, and because he committed a transgression, they fined him:

Rashi on Gittin 53a:4:3.hebrew: מדמע - לא מפסיד לגמרי, דהא חזי לכהנים וזבני מיניה בזול:
Rashi on Gittin 53a:4:3.english: One who mixes [terumah with non-sacred produce] - he does not ruin [it] completely, for [the mixture] is fit for priests, and they buy [it] from him cheaply:

Rashi on Gittin 53a:5:1.hebrew: משום דשכיח - דעביד, ובמילתא דשכיח עבדי רבנן תקנתא כי היכי דלא נעביד:
Rashi on Gittin 53a:5:1.english: Because it is common - that one does [it], and in a matter that is common, the Rabbis made an enactment so that one should not do [it]:

Rashi on Gittin 53a:6:1.english: Like Rabbi Yirmeya - for as soon as he lifted it, he acquired it:

Rashi on Gittin 53a:8:1.hebrew: למה לי - כיון דתנן מנסך בתרתי דרישא, כ"ש מדמע, דליכא למימר דקם ליה בדרבה מיניה:
Rashi on Gittin 53a:8:1.english: Why do I [need all these] - Since we learned [the case of] one who pours a libation among the first two [cases], all the more so [is one who] mixes [teruma into non-sacred produce liable], since one cannot say [regarding him] that he incurs the greater [penalty]:

Rashi on Gittin 53a:8:2.hebrew: מנסך - מפסיד לגמרי, שאוסרו בהנאה; אבל מטמא, אע"ג דמפסיד ליה לגמרי לענין שהוא עצמו אינו יכול לאכול, אבל חזי הוא עדיין להסקה או למאכל בהמה, דאפי' מטמא תרומה, חזי להסקה או לבהמת כהן:
Rashi on Gittin 53a:8:2.english: [One who] pours a libation - [He] causes a complete loss, for he renders it forbidden for [any] benefit; whereas [one who] renders [produce] impure, even though he causes him a complete loss insofar as he himself cannot eat [it], nevertheless it is still fit for fuel or for animal fodder, for even [if] he renders terumah impure, it is fit for fuel or for a kohen's animal:

Rashi on Gittin 53a:8:3.hebrew: מטמא, איכא הפסד מרובה, דלא חזיא תו לאכילה:
Rashi on Gittin 53a:8:3.english: [In the case of] one who renders [food] impure, there is a great loss, as it is no longer fit for eating:

Tosafot on Gittin 53a:15:1.hebrew: שלא יהא כל אחד ואחד כו' - הקשה ה"ר אפרים: הא דתנן בפרק עד כמה (בכורות דף כח:) "דן את הדין, טימא את הטהור — מה שעשה עשוי, וישלם מביתו", ואמאי? והא שוגג הוא! ומאן דמוקי לה כר"מ דדאין דינא דגרמי — ניחא, דלקמן קניס ר"מ שוגג אטו מזיד. אבל למאן דמוקי אפילו כרבנן, ובנגע בהו שרץ, קשה לר' יוחנן: אמאי חייב? ומיהו לחזקיה אתי שפיר, דלא שייך למיפטריה כדי שיודיעו. ותירץ: דהתם פשע, דמה היה לו לטמאותה כדי להחזיק דבריו? והוי כמו מזיד דהכא. וא"ת: בטיהר את הטמא, שעירבו עם פירותיו, לפטור לחזקיה כדי שיודיעו? ויש לומר: דאין רגילות שיחזור מהוראתו אלא ע"י אחרים, הלכך לא חיישינן:
Tosafot on Gittin 53a:15:1.english: So that each and every person [should not], etc. - Rabbi Ephraim raised a difficulty: That which we learned in the Mishnah in the chapter [entitled] Ad Kama (Bekhorot 28b): "[If one] judged a case, [or] declared the pure impure — what he did is done, and he must pay from his own pocket." But why [must he pay]? Surely he is an unintentional [offender]! Now, [according to] the one who establishes it as [following] Rabbi Meir, who adjudicates dina degarmi [liability for indirect causation of damage], it is well, for later [in our sugya] Rabbi Meir penalizes an unintentional [act] on account of an intentional [act]. However, according to the one who establishes [it] even as [following] the Rabbis, and [in a case] where [the judge] touched a sheretz [ritually impure creeping creature] to them, it is difficult for Rabbi Yoḥanan: why is he liable? However, according to Ḥizkiyah it works out well, for it is not relevant to exempt him in order that he inform [the owner]. And he answered: There he was negligent, for why did he have to render it impure in order to uphold his words? Thus it is like an intentional [act] here. And if you say: In [the case where he] declared the impure pure, where [the owner] mixed it with his [other] produce, let him be exempt according to Ḥizkiyah so that he inform [the owner]? One can say: It is not common for him to retract his ruling except through others; therefore we are not concerned [about that]:

Tosafot on Gittin 53a:16:1.hebrew: ותני עלה מפני תיקון העולם - ברוב ספרים גרסינן במתניתין: "הכהנים שפיגלו במקדש, שוגגין פטורין, מזידין חייבין". ופריך משום דמשמע ליה ד"מפני תיקון העולם" דקתני בברייתא קאי א"מזידין חייבין" דקתני לבסוף. והכי איתא בתוספתא [פ"ג]: "בראשונה היו אומרים: המטמא והמנסך, חזרו לומר: אף המדמע, בשוגג פטור, מזיד חייב מפני תיקון העולם; הכהנים שפגלו במקדש, שוגגין פטורין, מזידין חייבין מפני תקון העולם". וקשה, דמרישא ד"המטמא והמדמע והמנסך" דקיימי בהו הוה ליה למיפרך! לכך נראה דלא גרסינן במתני' "שוגגין פטורין", וברייתא דהכא לאו היינו דתוספתא דהתם שהבאתי, ו"מפני תיקון העולם" אדיוקא קאי. וכה"ג משני לקמן (גיטין דף נה:) אחטאת גזולה שלא נודעה לרבים:
Tosafot on Gittin 53a:16:1.english: And it is taught with regard to it: For the betterment of the world - In most editions, we have the reading in the Mishnah: "The priests who rendered [an offering] piggul in the Temple — [if they did so] unintentionally, they are exempt; [if] intentionally, they are liable." And [the Gemara] raises an objection because it understands that "for the betterment of the world," which is taught in the Baraita, refers to "intentionally, they are liable," which is taught at the end [of the Mishnah]. And thus it is stated in the Tosefta ([Chapter 3]): "Initially they would say: One who renders [another's produce] ritually impure and one who pours [another's wine as a libation]; they retracted [and] said: Even one who mixes [terumah into another's non-sacred produce] — [if] unintentionally, he is exempt; [if] intentionally, he is liable, for the betterment of the world. The priests who rendered [an offering] piggul in the Temple — [if] unintentionally, they are exempt; [if] intentionally, they are liable, for the betterment of the world." And this is difficult: for from the first clause of "one who renders impure, mixes, or pours [as a libation]," which [the Gemara] is currently discussing, it should have raised its objection! Therefore, it appears that we do not have the reading "unintentionally, they are exempt" in the Mishnah, and the Baraita [cited] here is not the same as that of the Tosefta there that I cited; rather, "for the betterment of the world" refers to the inference [from the Mishnah, i.e., that unintentionally they are exempt]. And similarly, [the Gemara] answers later (Gittin 55b) regarding a stolen sin-offering that was not known to the public:

Tosafot on Gittin 53a:19:1.hebrew: העושה מלאכה במי חטאת ובפרת חטאת - מעובד דומיא דעבד דרשינן דעלה עליה זכר פסולה, אע"ג דממילא, כיון דניחא להו לבעלים; וה"ה דכי עביד חבירו בידים וניחא ליה לאותו שעושה, דמיתרבי נמי מעובד מ"מ:
Tosafot on Gittin 53a:19:1.english: One who performs a task with the water of purification or with the heifer of purification - From [the term] "ubad" analogous to "avad" we expound that if a male mounted her she is disqualified, even though [it happened] on its own, since it is pleasing to the owners; and the same applies when his fellow does [labor with it] actively and it is pleasing to that one who does [it], for it is also included from "ubad" in any case:

Tosafot on Gittin 53a:19:2.hebrew: בדיני אדם נמי ליחייב - וא"ת: והרי צורם אוזן פרתו של חבירו דפטור, כדאמר בפ"ב דזבחים (כה:) ובהגוזל קמא (ב"ק צח.), משום דכולהו שוורין לאו לגבי מזבח קיימי; ופריך התם מהך דהעושה מלאכה — משמע דוקא מלאכה דלא מינכר הזיקא! ומשני: דנקט מלאכה לרבותא, דאע"ג דלא מינכר, מיחייב בדיני שמים. ונראה דהאי דסתם שוורים לאו לגבי מזבח קיימי, לא עביד ליה אלא כהיזק שאינו ניכר:
Tosafot on Gittin 53a:19:2.english: According to human laws he should also be liable - And if you ask: Behold, one who slits the ear of another's cow is exempt, as it says in the second chapter of Zevachim (25b) and in [the chapter] HaGozel Kamma (Bava Kamma 98a), because not all oxen stand for the altar; and there [the Gemara] asks from this [baraita] of "one who performs a task" — implying specifically [performing] a task, where the damage is not evident! And [the Gemara] answers that it stated "a task" to teach a novel point, that even though [the damage] is not evident, he is liable according to the laws of Heaven. And it appears that this [reason], that ordinary oxen do not stand for the altar, renders it only like damage that is not evident:

Tosafot on Gittin 53a:4:1.hebrew: משום דקא מפסיד ליה לגמרי - הך סוגיא כר' יוחנן, דאמר היזק שאינו ניכר אינו היזק; דלחזקיה הוה ליה לאצרוכיה לפטורא:
Tosafot on Gittin 53a:4:1.english: Because he ruins it entirely - This sugya [follows] Rabbi Yochanan, who says [that] unrecognizable damage is not [considered] damage; for according to Chizkiyah, [the Gemara] would have had to explain the necessity [of all three cases] with respect to the exemption:

Tosafot on Gittin 53a:8:1.hebrew: בראשונה היו אומרים המטמא והמנסך - בהגוזל בתרא (שם קיז.) כתובה אפכא, וזו אחת מסוגיות הפוכות:
Tosafot on Gittin 53a:8:1.english: Initially they would say: One who renders impure and one who pours - In [the chapter] HaGozel Batra (there, 117a) it is written the opposite way, and this is one of the inverted sugyot:
